description: making a website for  Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map
summary: MARSWALK is a browser-based Mars exploration and route-planning workspace developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map" challenge.   What was developed: A zero-backend web application featuring an interactive Leaflet mapping engine that integrates NASA Trek Viking imagery and MGS MOLA elevation relief. It includes a great-circle route planner with custom waypoints, real-time MOLA elevation profile charts, a curated science landmarks database, and a one-click mission briefing generator that exports to PDF, JSON, and CSV.   How it addresses the challenge: It translates complex planetary datasets into an intuitive interface, allowing explorers to plot paths between landing sites and science targets across a spherical Mars while instantly calculating distance, climb, descent, and regional gradients.   Why it is important: MARSWALK bridges raw orbital data and mission planning while championing radical data honesty. Rather than presenting unverified paths or hiding coarse-grid limitations, the tool explicitly communicates resolution constraints and terrain uncertainties—ensuring decision-makers understand both what the data shows and what it cannot capture.
details:
1. What it does & How it works

MARSWALK is a lightweight, client-side web application running entirely in the browser with no backend requirements. Users can explore Mars using planetocentric coordinates (latitude and east-positive longitude, 0–360° E).

  • Interactive Mapping: Powered by Leaflet, the application integrates NASA Trek WMTS Viking color mosaic imageryand MGS MOLA elevation relief tiles, featuring an automatic fallback to a coordinate grid if external tiles are unreachable.
  • Spherical Routing & Profiling: Users click the map to define start points, intermediate waypoints, and destinations. The app computes great-circle paths on a spherical Mars ($R = 3389.5\text{ km}$)and samples downsampled USGS/PDS MOLA topography grids (mola_grid.json)to generate elevation profile charts, total climb/descent metrics, and flat-ground walking time estimates.
  • Mission Briefings: Automatically compiles route telemetry, elevation ranges, and nearby landmarks within 500 km into a structured report that can be printed as a PDF or exported as JSON and CSV.

2. Key Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Accessibility: Eliminates the need for heavy desktop GIS software, putting planetary exploration data directly into an accessible web interface.
  • Transparency in Planning: Fosters rigorous mission conceptualization by making geospatial analysis straightforward for students, researchers, and space enthusiasts.

3. Technology Stack & Data Sources

  • Frontend Languages & Frameworks: Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, and CSS3 (utilizing modern CSS Grid/Flexbox and custom dark-themed aerospace styling).
  • Mapping Library: Leaflet.js (v1.9.4).
  • Data Sources: NASA Trek WMTS services (Viking MDIM 2.1 mosaic and MGS MOLA relief), USGS/PDS MOLA gridded topography, and IAU reference feature datasets.

4. Design Philosophy: Radical Honesty

A core pillar of MARSWALK is avoiding false confidence in planetary data:

  • Direct great-circle routes are never labeled as "safe paths".
  • Coarse MOLA elevation grids are explicitly noted to lack rover- or human-scale resolution (ignoring local boulders, small craters, and local micro-slopes).
  • Unconfigured or unreachable layers (such as CRISM mineral data slots) are transparently labeled rather than simulated.
